note: Situations and the applicability entry ids that apply to each, under the International rules. The two-subject sibling of applicability-fixtures.json, which is untouched and stays the one-subject contract (REQ-VERIFY-1, REQ-CAT-5). A situation addresses each vessel's facts through the subject namespace of docs/identifiers.md: <subject>:<class>:<key>, subject in {own, other, pair}.

expect_form.note: An element of `expect` is either a bare entry id, exactly as in applicability-fixtures.json, or an object {"entry": <id>, "modality": <modality>} naming the modality that entry is expected to carry for this situation. The two forms are interchangeable and a bare id asserts nothing about modality, so the published one-subject fixtures remain valid unedited while Q-5's three modality-only gates (23a2, 26b-mast, 30c) become fixturable.

case_status.note: `status` says whether a case asserts anything. `illustrative` cases fix the shape of the situation record and the namespace before any two-subject entry exists; nothing in Part B is modelled yet, so their `expect` is empty and the test suite checks their shape and namespace resolution only. A case becomes `binding` when the entries it names exist, and only then does it join the fixture replay.

cases.name: crossing: own power-driven, other fine on the starboard bow
cases.narrative: Two power-driven vessels in sight of one another, other bearing 040 relative at 3 nm on a steady bearing and crossing right to left ahead. Own has the other on her own starboard side, so own is the give-way vessel under Rule 15 and Rule 16 governs the action; the other is stand-on under Rule 17. Rule 15 is not transcribed yet, so this asserts nothing.
expect_when_modelled: 7(d)(i) risk of collision from the steady bearing

cases.name: narrow channel: head-on round a bend, bank 100 m to starboard
cases.narrative: The R1 illustration of ADR 0005 sec. 5 and the proposal's sec. 4. Own keeps to the starboard side of a narrow channel per Rule 9(a); a vessel cuts the bend and is head-on at 800 m. Rule 14(a) requires each to alter to starboard, and the bank is 100 m to starboard of own. Every compliant plan grounds or collides; a port alteration passes starboard-to-starboard and breaches 14(a). The value of the case here is not the region finding, which belongs to colregs-engine -- it is that the situation record can carry it at all.
expect_when_modelled: 2(b) region, computed in colregs-engine and never an entry here
cases.gap: There is no fact for 'in a narrow channel or fairway', because Rule 9 is not transcribed and no scope fact class exists yet. When one lands it is a scope fact of the situation, not of either vessel, and belongs beside pair.geo rather than in either fact record. Recorded here so the omission is visible rather than inferred.

cases.name: 13(d) latch: an overtaking whose bearing has drawn out to a crossing
cases.narrative: Own came up on the other vessel from abaft her beam and is overtaking. The bearing has since drawn out: own now bears 250 relative from the other, just outside Rule 13(b)'s 112.5-247.5 sector, so the instantaneous geometry alone would reclassify this as a crossing with the other vessel give-way. Rule 13(d) forbids exactly that, and own:hist:was_overtaking is the fact that carries it. This is the case that makes history a class rather than a note.
